name: MODIS Combined Land Cover (MCD12Q1) IGBP classification, 2023
source_org: NASA LP DAAC, via NASA GIBS

name: Gridded Population of the World v4, population density 2020
source_org: NASA SEDAC (CIESIN, Columbia University), via NASA GIBS
limitations: Modelled from census inputs. The GIBS colour map is binned and its top bin is ≥ 1,000 people/km², so values are capped at 1,000.

name: VIIRS Black Marble night lights, 2016 composite
source_org: NASA Earth Observatory / NASA GIBS
limitations: A visual RGB composite, not calibrated radiance. Values are relative brightness 0–255.
method: Luminance (0.2126 R + 0.7152 G + 0.0722 B) averaged over the hex.

source_org: NASA SEDAC (CIESIN / World Bank / UNEP / NGI), via NASA GIBS
limitations: Old observation periods (1980–2003). Use only for broad patterns.
method: Colour decoded to the class value; open top classes take their lower bound; averaged over the hex.

# census2011_district and census2011_state

Build script: `pipeline/build_census2011.py`. Fetch script: `pipeline/fetch_population.py`.

## Source
- Used: GitHub mirror `nishusharma1608/India-Census-2011-Analysis`, file `india-districts-census-2011.csv`. It is the same file as Kaggle `danofer/india-census`. It is a compilation of the official Census 2011 Primary Census Abstract and houselisting tables.
- Not reached: the official Census site. `https://censusindia.gov.in` returns a redirect to `census.website` and the table files are not direct downloads. I did not try the Census Digital Library or `censuscode.gov.in`. The mirror's national total (1,210,854,977) equals the official total. The mirror values are not checked against the official files.

## Coverage
- District rows: 640 of 640 source rows match `data/ref/districts2011.csv` by censuscode (100 percent).
- The reference file has 641 rows. The one unmatched reference row is censuscode 0 ("Data Not Available"). It is a placeholder, not a district.
- 13 district names differ in spelling between the mirror and the reference (for example Mahrajganj/Maharajganj). The join uses the code only.
- State rows: 36 (all states and UTs of today). Sum of population = 1,210,854,977.
- Telangana: 10 districts of 2011 Andhra Pradesh (codes 532-541) map to TG. Ladakh: Leh and Kargil map to LA. Daman, Diu, Dadra and Nagar Haveli map to DH. Each district row has `state` (today) and `state_2011`.

## Gaps in the source
- No area, no 0-6 population, no urban population. `literacy_rate` is literate persons per 100 of the total population (all ages). It is not the official rate. Urban share is given for households only.
- Age groups are 0-29, 30-49 and 50+ only.
- The education-level counts cover a subset of persons (`edu_total`). Use `pct_graduate` only with that denominator.
- Senapati (Manipur): the worker-category counts do not sum to total workers in the source. Values are kept as they are.
- The mirror has other household columns (water, latrine, fuel, assets) that this dataset does not include.

## Optional dataset not built
- `growth` / `migration` (2001 to 2011 decadal growth): not built. No 2001 district table was fetched.

# census_district_series

Dataset: `data/normalized/census_district_series.json`. Resolution: `district2011_year`. Kind: official.
Build: `pipeline/fetch_census_series.py`, `pipeline/build_census_series.py`.

## Source
Census of India 2011, Table A-2 "Decadal variation in population since 1901". The Census publishes one file per state at district level on 2011 boundaries.
Catalog pages: `https://censusindia.gov.in/nada/index.php/catalog/43333` (India) to `/43368` (Andaman and Nicobar Islands). Catalog id = 43333 + state code.
The fetch script reads the download link on each page (xls or xlsx). Raw files: `raw/census_series/a2_xlsx/NN.xls(x)`, NN = Census state code (00 = India).
Columns used: Persons, Males, Females. The file of Andhra Pradesh holds the 10 districts of Telangana. The file of Jammu and Kashmir holds Leh and Kargil (Ladakh). The state id comes from `census2011_district.json`.

## Coverage
- 640 districts x 12 census years (1901-2011) = 7680 rows. All 640 districts of `census2011_district` match. Unmatched source rows: none.
- 421 rows have a null population: 394 are `N.A` in the source (districts without a past value, mostly Arunachal Pradesh, Mizoram, Delhi, Punjab, Manipur, Haryana, Sikkim, Nagaland, 1901-1951), and 27 are Assam 1981 (see breaks).
- Null counts by year: 1901 69, 1911 69, 1921 69, 1931 69, 1941 68, 1951 40, 1961 10, 1981 27. Years 1971, 1991, 2001, 2011 are complete.
- The column `flag` holds the reason for each null.

## Checks (district sum against the national row of Table A-2)
| Year | District sum | India row | Difference |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1951 | 359,010,091 | 361,088,090 | 2,077,999 (null districts) |
| 1971 | 548,159,652 | 548,159,652 | 0 |
| 1991 | 846,421,039 | 846,421,039 | 0 |
| 2001 | 1,028,737,436 | 1,028,737,436 | 0 |
| 2011 | 1,210,854,977 | 1,210,854,977 | 0 |

- 2011 sum equals 1,210,854,977 exactly. This equals the Census 2011 total.
- The India row for 1951 is 361,088,090 (official about 361.1 M). The India row for 2001 is 1,028,737,436 (official about 1,028.7 M). The district sums are lower in 1951 because of null districts. The state series (`census_state_series`) uses official state rows and matches both national totals exactly.
- Differences in 1901-1941, 1961 and 1981 come from null districts (and Assam 1981).

## Known breaks
- Past populations are adjusted by the Census to 2011 boundaries. The adjustment method is the Census own method. No re-check is done here.
- Assam 1981: the census was not held. The source has no district value ("---"). The state row has a value that the Census interpolated. The district rows stay null.
- Andhra Pradesh: for 1901, 1911, 1921 and 1931 the district totals differ from the state row (-21,599; -70,744; +16,456; +8,240). The Census explains this in a note: an error in Table A-2 of 1941 for Medak and Nizamabad. The district values are copied as published.
- Actual census years differ from the nominal year in some units. Column `year_actual` holds them: Goa, Daman, Diu, Dadra and Nagar Haveli (1900, 1910, 1940, 1950, 1960; Dadra and Nagar Haveli 1961 = 1962) and Puducherry, Karaikal, Mahe, Yanam (1951 = 1948).
- 1901 state male and female figures of Madhya Pradesh are estimates in the Census table. District values are not touched.
- Italic districts (formed after 2001) are normal rows here.

## Sources tried and not reached
- None failed for this dataset. Every catalog page 43333-43368 returned a file.

name: Census of India - state and UT series 1901-2011 (population, sex ratio, urban share, literacy)
source_org: Office of the Registrar General & Census Commissioner, India (Census of India); Ministry of Finance (Economic Survey 2021-22); MoSPI (SSES 2017)
url: https://censusindia.gov.in/nada/index.php/catalog/43333 (Table A-2, one catalog page per state)
limitations: Population, males and females are on 2011 boundaries (Table A-2). Urban share and literacy for 1951-2001 are on the state boundaries of each census year (states formed in 2000 are recast by the Census). They stay null for AP, TG, JK, LA and DH before 2011 because these boundaries changed. Urban share exists for 1991, 2001 and 2011 only. 2011 urban share and literacy come from district counts on present boundaries. Literacy age basis changes: 1951-1971 age 5+, 1981 onward age 7+. Assam 1981 and J&K 1991 values in the Census are interpolated by the Census. No value is estimated by this pipeline.
method: Population: official state row of Table A-2, except AP, TG, JK, LA (sum of districts when every district has a value) and DH (sum of the two UT rows). Sex ratio = females per 1000 males from the same rows. Urban share 2011 = urban population / population from census2011_district. Literacy 2011 = literate / (population - age 0-6) from census2011_district. Literacy 1951-2001 and urban share 1991-2001: published tables as listed in the coverage note.
redistributed_via: Economic Survey 2021-22 and SSES 2017 are Government of India publications that republish Census tables.

# census_state_series

Dataset: `data/normalized/census_state_series.json`. Resolution: `state_year`. 36 states and UTs x 12 census years (1901-2011) = 432 rows. Kind: official.
Build: `pipeline/build_census_state_series.py` (needs `census_district_series.json` and `census2011_district.json`).

## Sources and tables
- Population, males, females, sex ratio: Census 2011 Table A-2 (2011 boundaries). State row of each state file. See `census_district_series.md`.
  - AP and TG, JK and LA: sum of A-2 district rows, only when every district has a value in that year. Both AP and TG are complete for all years.
  - DH (Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu): sum of the two UT rows of A-2.
  - Sex ratio = females per 1000 males (rounded) from the same rows.
- Literacy rate 1951-2001: Economic Survey 2021-22, Statistical Appendix Table 8.5 "State-wise literacy rates (1951-2011)". Source note: Registrar General of India. Raw: `raw/census_series/es_pages/page621.html` (URL `https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/ebook_es2022/files/basic-html/page621.html`). A second copy (2020-21 Table 9.4, page906) is also saved but not used.
- Literacy rate 2011 and urban population and share 2011: computed from the 2011 district counts in `census2011_district.json` on present boundaries (literacy = literate / (population - age 0-6), age 7+).
- Urban share 1991 and 2001: MoSPI "Selected Socio-Economic Statistics India 2017", Table 1.7 (source: Registrar General of India). URL `https://mospi.gov.in/sites/default/files/publication_reports/SelectedSocio-EconomicStatisticsIndia2017_27oct17.pdf`, PDF page 20. The PDF text layer is garbled, so the values are read by eye from the page image and typed into `URBAN_TABLE` in the build script. The 2011 column of the same table is checked against the district sums (see checks).
- Table A-4 is not used for urban values. A-4 lists towns of 2011 with their past population. A sum of these is not the urban population of past years.

## Checks
- National sums of the state rows: 1951 = 361,088,090; 2001 = 1,028,737,436; 2011 = 1,210,854,977. All equal the India row of A-2 (official about 361.1 M, 1,028.7 M, 1,210.9 M).
- For states that have their own A-2 file, the state row equals the sum of the district rows in every year where all districts have a value: 0 mismatches.
- 2011 urban share (district sum) against the MoSPI table: equal within 0.06 points for all states except AP (29.58 against 33.36: the table includes Telangana), DH (58.51 against 46.72 and 75.17: the table lists the two UTs apart) and JK (27.48 against 27.38: the table includes Ladakh). This also supports the hand transcription.
- 2011 literacy (district derived) against Economic Survey: equal within 0.06 points except AP (67.41 against 67.0) and JK (67.0 against 67.2). Same boundary reasons.

## Definitions and breaks
- Literacy age basis is in `literacy_age_basis`: "5+" for 1951, 1961, 1971; "7+" for 1981 onward. West Bengal 1951 includes ages 0-4. Do not compare the two bases without care.
- Literacy 1951 of Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh and Manipur is based on a sample (flag). Manipur 2001 excludes three sub-divisions of Senapati district (cancelled census).
- Population is on 2011 boundaries. Literacy 1951-2001 and urban share 1991-2001 are on the state boundaries of the census year as published (the Census recasts Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Uttarakhand). For states with a boundary change (AP, TG, JK, LA, DH) these values are left null before 2011. The published values exist for AP (with Telangana), JK (with Ladakh), Daman and Diu and Dadra and Nagar Haveli (apart) but do not match present boundaries.
- Assam 1981: the Census did not count. The state population is interpolated by the Census (flag). The Economic Survey has no literacy value for Assam 1981 (null). J&K 1991: census not held; Census values are interpolated (JK 1991 population is a district sum from A-2 and is not flagged here; the interpolation note of the Census applies).
- Puducherry 1951 slot is the census of 1948 (`year_actual` = 1948). Goa, Daman, Diu and DNH use 1900/1910/1940/1950/1960 (DNH 1962).
- Telangana (2014), Ladakh (2019) and DH (2020) are shown for all years on present boundaries. TG and LA come from district sums. DH comes from the two UT rows.

## Gaps (null cells)
- Population: Arunachal Pradesh 1901-1951 (source N.A). Sex ratio: Madhya Pradesh 1901, Puducherry 1901, 1931, 1941 (no male or female split in the source), and Arunachal Pradesh 1901-1951.
- Urban share: all states for 1901-1981 (no state table found on a usable route), and AP, TG, JK, LA, DH for 1991 and 2001. Present for 1991, 2001, 2011 for 31 states and UTs and for 2011 for all 36.
- Literacy: all states for 1901-1941. Null in 1951-2001 where the Economic Survey says na: AR 1951; AS 1981; CH 1951, 1961; DL 1951; HR 1951, 1961; HP 1951-1981; KA 1951; ML 1951; PY 1951; PB 1951, 1961; SK 1951, 1961; TN 1951; TR 1951; plus AP, TG, JK, LA, DH 1951-2001 (boundary rule). 2011 is complete for all 36.

- `https://rbidocs.rbi.org.in/rdocs/Publications/PDFs/6TABLE4134B659E3B243EE9CB292D36ABC281B.PDF` (RBI Handbook, Table 6 literacy): same CAPTCHA page.
- `https://mohua.gov.in/pdf/5c80e2225a124Handbook%20of%20Urban%20Statistics%202019.pdf`: HTTP 200 but the body is an HTML page, not a PDF.

# cities

Build script: `pipeline/build_cities.py`. Fetch script: `pipeline/fetch_population.py`.

## Sources
- Population: English Wikipedia tables that cite Census of India 2011. They are fetched with the MediaWiki parse API.
  - `List of million-plus urban agglomerations in India` gives `ua_population_2011` (52 rows).
  - `List of cities in India by population` gives `city_population_2011`.
- Coordinates and QIDs: Wikidata. The Wikipedia pageprops API gives the QID. The Wikidata `wbgetentities` API gives property P625. All 112 rows use Wikidata P625. The script has fallbacks (Wikipedia coordinates API, then the Wikipedia table) that were not needed.
- Not reached: official Census UA tables (PDF/XLS) were not tried. The WDQS SPARQL endpoint was not used.

## Coverage
- 112 rows. 34 are state/UT/national capitals (36 jurisdictions: Chandigarh serves Chandigarh, Punjab and Haryana; New Delhi serves Delhi and India). 52 rows have a UA population. All 112 rows have coordinates, state, QID, `census2011_district` and `district2020`.
- Rows with no UA population are cities that are not million-plus (for example Guwahati, Bhubaneswar, Dehradun). They have `city_population_2011` where the Wikipedia city table has it.
- Capitals with no Census population in the source: Daman, Dispur (inside Guwahati UA), Gangtok, Itanagar, Kavaratti, Kohima, Leh, Panaji, Port Blair, Puducherry, Shillong. They have null population.
- Amaravati: the Wikipedia city table has 103,000. This is not a Census 2011 count, so `city_population_2011` is null.
- Mumbai, Bengaluru, Kolkata and other rows: `city_population_2011` can be the municipal city only. Jaipur, Ludhiana and some others repeat the UA value in the Wikipedia table.
- Kerala UA figures are inflated by a changed UA definition in 2011.
- Core district: the `census2011_district` of a multi-district city is one district (Delhi = Central, Mumbai = Mumbai, satellite towns of Mumbai = Thane). `district2020` uses `dt_code` of `districts2020.csv`, with fixed overrides for Delhi, Asansol, Durgapur and Vasai-Virar.

name: District-wise area, production and yield of major crops, 2022-23
source_org: Directorate of Economics & Statistics, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (APY portal)
limitations: Source reports 2022-23 district totals from the states. Some states report few districts or leave crops blank (null). # crop_district: district crop area, production, yield, 2022-23

Files: data/normalized/crop_district.json. Scripts: pipeline/fetch_apy.py, pipeline/build_crop_district.py. Resolution: district2020 (key `State|District`).

## Source
DES portal data.desagri.gov.in (public web forms, same data as the APY reports). Year 2022-23 is the latest year on the portal. Crops: rice, wheat, maize, cotton (lint, bales of 170 kg), sugarcane, and the groups cereals and millets, total pulses, total oilseeds, foodgrains.
The portal certificate chain is incomplete for Python. The fetch script uses verify=False for this public read-only data.

## Why district2020
The portal uses current district names (2022-23, after new districts). district2020 matches 700 of 737 source districts. district2011 would match fewer.

## Coverage
- Source districts: 737. Matched: 700 (exact 606, renamed by a hand table 64, close spelling 30). Unmatched: 37.
- Rows by field (non-null): rice 639, wheat 536, maize 618, pulses 675, oilseeds 686, sugarcane 481, cotton 285.
- `listed_foodgrain_prod_t` = rice + wheat + maize + total pulses. It leaves out jowar, bajra, ragi, barley, small millets. It is null when one of the four is null (for example no wheat). It is not the official foodgrain total. Rows with a value: 454.
- The fields `cereals_*` and `foodgrains_*` are the totals that the portal gives (all crops of the group).

## Quality notes
- National sums of the district values are higher than the official 2022-23 estimates: rice 148.6 Mt (official 135.8), wheat 128.2 Mt (official 110.6), foodgrains 357.8 Mt (official 330.5). District figures come from the states and differ from the national estimates. Use them for the spatial pattern, not for national totals.
- Blank values in the source are null. A crop that a district does not report is null, not zero.

license: Wikidata: CC0. Historical-basemaps geometry: GPL-3.0 (derived extents keep GPL-3.0). Era summaries: written by this project; sources cited per era.

method: Places and capitals are chosen in pipeline/history_config.py and resolved to Wikidata QIDs from English Wikipedia titles (redirects followed) to get coordinates. Dates are curated from the cited articles. # history (historical timeline layer)

File: `data/normalized/history.json` (kind `historical`, about 115 KB).
Scripts: `pipeline/history_config.py` (curated selection), `pipeline/fetch_history.py`, `pipeline/build_history.py`.
Run: `.venv/bin/python -I pipeline/fetch_history.py` then `.venv/bin/python -I pipeline/build_history.py`.
This layer is separate from modern statistics. Do not join it to census or economic data.

## Content (counts)
15 eras, 51 polities, 69 capital entries, 218 places, 37 polities with an extent polygon, 4 routes.
Eras: Indus Valley Civilisation; Vedic period; Mahajanapadas; Maurya Empire; post-Maurya kingdoms; Gupta Empire;
Pallava dynasty and early Deccan kingdoms; Chola Empire with Chalukya and Rashtrakuta; Delhi Sultanate;
Vijayanagara Empire with Bahmani and Deccan sultanates; Mughal Empire; Maratha Empire; Sikh Empire;
Colonial India; Independence and modern India (key dates only: 1947, 1950, 1956).

## Sources and licences
| Source | Use | Licence |
|---|---|---|
| Wikidata (https://query.wikidata.org/sparql) | QIDs, English labels, coordinates (P625) | CC0 |
| English Wikipedia API (https://en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php) | Title to QID, redirect resolution; article URLs; dating references | CC BY-SA 4.0 (only titles and URLs are used; no text is copied) |
| aourednik/historical-basemaps (https://github.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps), `geojson/world_*.geojson` | Polity extents | GPL-3.0. Derived extents keep GPL-3.0. Licence text is in `raw/history/LICENSE-historical-basemaps.txt`. |
| Britannica and Wikipedia articles listed per era | Era dates; summaries are written by this project | Cited only |

Basemap files used: bc2000, bc1000, bc500, bc200, 100, 400, 600, 700, 800, 1000, 1100, 1300, 1500, 1530, 1700, 1783, 1815, 1880, 1960.

## Method
- Places and capitals are chosen by hand in `history_config.py`. Each one is resolved from its English Wikipedia title
  (redirects followed; disambiguation pages are rejected) to a Wikidata QID. Coordinates come from Wikidata P625.
  Capitals of the polities were checked against Wikidata P36 (for example Pataliputra, Amaravati, Agra, Fatehpur Sikri, Bidar, Penukonda).
- Dates are rounded values from the cited articles. Negative years are BCE (1 BCE = -1; no year 0). `null` means unknown.
- Extents: basemap features are matched by exact NAME, unioned, clipped to lon 60-100 and lat 5-40, simplified at 0.05 degrees,
  rounded to 2 decimals. Parts under 0.01 square degrees are dropped. Confidence is `low` if the basemap year is before 1000 CE, else `medium`.
  If the basemap has no matching polygon, `geometry` is `null` and `confidence` is `null`. No outline is drawn by hand.
- Routes: polylines through the Wikidata coordinates of documented waypoint cities. They are not surveyed paths.

## Uncertainty notes
- The basemap shows one snapshot year per file. The snapshot year differs from `peak_year` (for example Maurya: 200 BCE map, peak about 250 BCE;
  Maratha: 1783 map, peak about 1760; Chola: 1000 map, peak about 1030). Each extent note says so.
- Ancient and medieval states had no fixed borders. Border lines show the basemap author's generalisation.
- The basemap name `Satavahanihara` is spelled so in the source. The match of `Saka Kingdom` to the Western Satraps is a reading by this project.
- `Vedic Aryans` (basemap) is a culture area, not a state. It is listed as "Vedic culture area (not a state)".
- Sites linked to legend (Kurukshetra and the Mahabharata) and to tradition (Buddha sites, Bodh Gaya, Lumbini) carry that remark in `note`.
- Indus sites: dates are approximate ranges. Mehrgarh and Bhirrana start before the Indus era and are precursors.
- Basemap before 1000 CE: confidence `low` for all extents.

## Coverage report (polities without an extent, `geometry` null)
- Mahajanapadas: Anga, Vajji, Chedi, Matsya, Assaka, Kamboja (no polygon in the basemap).
- Shunga, Harsha's realm, Sikh Empire (the basemap has no Sikh polygon in 1815 or nearby years), Bahmani Sultanate
  (the 1500 map has only a tiny remnant), Bengal, Bombay and Madras Presidencies and Hyderabad State (no provincial boundaries in the basemap).
- Polities with `qid` null have no QID in the file. They are listed by name only.
- Four battles were dropped because Wikidata has no coordinates: Battle of Takkolam, Battle of Pratapgad, Battle of Chillianwala, Battle of Gujrat.
  Some other battle coordinates are those of the nearest town or site and are approximate.
- Wikidata `Q389755` (Pataliputra) and similar are used by QID where the English title is not unique.

## Sources not used / problems
- The Wikidata `wbsearchentities` API did not return JSON to curl; SPARQL and the Wikipedia API were used instead.
- The QIDs in the task list for Indus (Q11954), Vijayanagara (Q1053347), Delhi Sultanate (Q130336), Sikh Empire (Q83891) and Pallava (Q1052961)
  were wrong (they point to unrelated items). Correct QIDs used: Indus Valley Civilization Q42534, Vijayanagara Empire Q167639,
  Delhi Sultanate Q229411, Sikh Empire Q83572, Pallava dynasty Q466803. The others were verified by label.
- The Wikipedia API returned HTTP 429 on rapid calls; the fetch script waits between calls.

NFHS-5 (2019-21) district fact sheet indicators. Built by `pipeline/build_health.py` (fetch: `pipeline/fetch_health.py`).

## Source
Mirror of the official IIPS/MoHFW PDF fact sheets: `jvargh7/nfhs5_factsheets` (MIT licence), 705 districts, 104 indicators. Cross-check: `pratapvardhan/NFHS-5` (CC BY 4.0, 341 districts from 21 states): 34,134 of 34,422 shared values agree (99.2 percent). The differences are in a few duplicate-numbered or parse-damaged rows and were not investigated one by one.
The mirror `pratapvardhan/NFHS-5` alone is not enough: it has no Phase 2 states (UP, MP, Rajasthan, Odisha and others).

## Coverage
- Source districts: 705. Matched to districts2020.csv: 693 (98.3 percent of source). Output rows: 693 of 724 districts2020 rows (95.7 percent of districts2020 rows have data).
- Unmatched source rows (12), left out on purpose: the 11 Delhi districts (districts2020.csv has one row, "Delhi") and Maharashtra "Mumbai Suburban" (not in districts2020.csv). NFHS "Mumbai" (the island city) matches the name "Mumbai" (code 519, the only Mumbai polygon in raw/boundaries) and is kept. Caveat: if that polygon covers the suburban area too, the value describes only part of it.
- districts2020 rows with no data (31): created after NFHS-5 (Arunachal: Kamle, Lepa Rada, Lower Siang, Pakke Kessang, Shi Yomi; Gujarat: Vav-Tharad; MP: Niwari; Manipur: 7 new districts; Mizoram: Hnahthial, Khawzawl; Tamil Nadu: 5 new districts; Telangana: Mulugu, Narayanpet; West Bengal: Alipurduar, Jhargram, Kalimpong), Chandigarh and Lakshadweep (no district fact sheet), Delhi, and J&K Mirpur and Muzaffarabad (not surveyed).

- Districts that were split after NFHS-5 keep the parent's value on the parent name only. Boundaries of the parent changed, so the value describes the old area.

## Indicators
31 indicators chosen by NFHS fact sheet number (see `IND` in the build script). `higher_is` is set for each field. Values of "Percentage not shown; based on fewer than 25 unweighted cases" are null. Values flagged "Based on 25-49 unweighted cases" are kept.

name: Hidden strengths (district2011)
source_org: India Civ model (pipeline/strengths.py)
method: Hidden strengths: districts and states that do better than their conditions predict.  Each model fits an ordinary least-squares line: outcome ~ conditions (all standardised). The residual, divided by the residual standard deviation, is the score: +1.5 means "1.5 standard deviations better than places with the same conditions". The sign is flipped for outcomes where lower is better (stunting), so a positive score is always good.  The scores go into derived datasets (strengths_district2011, strengths_district2020, strengths_state) that the normal lens, table and source code then publishes.
limitations: A residual is not a cause. Conditions that a model leaves out (irrigation, history, policy, data error) also give large residuals. Inputs of different years are named in each field.
